title: What Happens to Your Body When You Exercise?
paragraphs: As soon as you start moving, your body reacts. Your heart beats faster and you breathe more deeply, so that more oxygen reaches your muscles. Blood vessels in the muscles open wider to let more blood in.

Muscles turn oxygen and stored fuel, such as sugar and fat, into energy. This process also produces heat, which is why your body temperature rises and you begin to sweat. Sweat cools the skin as it dries.

Exercise affects the brain as well. It increases blood flow to the brain and releases chemicals that can improve mood and reduce stress. Regular activity is also linked to better sleep and better memory.

Over weeks and months, the heart becomes more efficient and muscles and bones get stronger. The World Health Organization recommends that adults do at least 150 minutes of moderate activity, such as brisk walking, each week, and some muscle-strengthening exercise twice a week.
